item.description:
Quieter reviews, more reliable deletion

  • Uncertain agent results now stay in Agents → Activity without adding a Gmail label. A Needs review filter makes them easier to find. Existing review labels are left unchanged.
  • Clearly unrelated email no longer becomes a review solely because an attachment could not be read. Uncertain or incomplete matches still require review before an agent acts.
  • ⌘Delete can queue emails while Cove is busy. The notification distinguishes waiting from an active Gmail request, and Undo remains available until the request starts.
  • Deleting another email while a previous deletion is being sent keeps a separate undo window. Long waits restore the affected emails with an error instead of leaving a stuck notification.

A home for your agents’ categories

  • Categories now has its own page. Search your agents’ labels, see downloaded and unread counts, and open a category to browse its emails.
  • Only labels configured in your agents or actually applied by them appear here. Fixed example shortcuts such as Purchases, Work, and Newsletters have been removed.
  • Email rows show your agents’ applied labels instead of built-in category names. Existing Gmail labels remain editable in the reader.
  • Follow-up flags and Jev’s assessments remain separate from Categories.

Your labels and follow-ups, together

  • Browse Gmail labels in Cove, including labels applied by your agents. Label views include inbox and archived mail, with search, unread filtering, sorting, and older messages loaded from Gmail.
  • Add or remove an email’s labels in the reader. When a Cove agent applied a label, the reader shows which agent did it.
  • Flag emails for follow-up from the list, reader, or Home. These flags sync with Gmail’s stars and appear in the Flagged view.
  • Jev’s saved assessments now appear as Needs action, Time-sensitive, and Review category badges, with dedicated sidebar views. These assessments remain separate from your manual follow-up flags.

Jev flags and displayed counts reflect downloaded mail. Open a label and load older mail to browse more of its messages.
